thread:
Sam (ACME): Hey team — were seeing intermittent disconnects from your streaming SSE endpoint. Connections drop after ~15-40s, clients reconnect and sometimes get duplicated events or a truncated last event. Can you help?
Maya (support): Sorry to hear that. Can you paste a minimal request + client stack? Also are you seeing HTTP 5xx or specific socket errors on the client?
Sam (ACME): Wem using eventsource polyfill (node-fetch) behind a corporate proxy (BlueShield). No 5xx, client logs show ECONNRESET and then a partial chunk arrives. Quick curl we used:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate?model=rwft"
```
Maya (support): Thanks. Two common suspects: (1) corporate proxies that buffer and then drop idle or slow connections; (2) slow consumer on the client causing kernel send buffer to fill and our runtime to hit EAGAIN/EPIPE and close the stream. Can you paste client trace when ECONNRESET appears?
Sam (ACME): Client stack (trimmed):
```
Error: read ECONNRESET
    at TCP.onStreamRead (internal/stream_base_commons.js:201:27)
```
Luis (backend): If the app processes events slowly (heavy CPU/blocking parse) the TCP receive window closes and our writes will get EAGAIN on non-blocking sockets. Historically that leads to either graceful backpressure handling or, if writes keep failing, a backpressure timeout where we close the connection to protect the worker. Do you notice whether the last event body is truncated or re-emitted on reconnect?
Sam (ACME): Both. Sometimes the final event is split mid-line and on reconnect we see the end repeated — duplication.
Priya (runtime): For SSE we rely on incremental flushes and short writes; proxies that coalesce chunks can turn many small flushes into one big frame. That defeats per-chunk progress and pushes our write buffer to fill. On the server we log EAGAIN/EPIPE in that case. We also encountered SIGPIPE aborts from a downstream HTTP lib in an older deploy and had to patch to ignore SIGPIPE and surface write errors via return codes instead.
Maya (support): Short repro steps to help isolate:
1) Try direct connection (no proxy) with a fast consumer: `curl -N ... | pv -qL 10000` should be stable.
2) Run a slow reader: `curl -N ... | pv -qL 10` (very slow) and tail server logs for EAGAIN/EPIPE/backpressure warnings.
3) If you can, capture pcap: `tcpdump -w client.pcap host api.redwood.ai` to inspect TCP windows and reassembly.
Sam (ACME): We tried those. No proxy + fast consumer = stable. With slow reader behind the BlueShield proxy we reproduce the disconnects. I grabbed a server log snippet you shared: 
```
[redwood-stream][INFO] write attempt: req=0x1a2b size=8192 wrote=4096 err=EAGAIN
[redwood-stream][WARN] backpressure timeout exceeded for req=0x1a2b, closing stream
```
Priya (runtime): That log indicates our per-request send retry loop hit the configured timeout. To prevent a single slow client from blocking GPU workers we close the connection after the backpressure window. When the socket dies mid-frame, some bytes may already have been flushed; the client can therefore receive a truncated event and then on reconnect we may resume by resending the last chunk which looks like duplication.
Maya (support): Practical mitigations while we debug:
- Bypass/whitelist the proxy if possible so it doesn't buffer.
- Make the client reader non-blocking: read network data and push into an in-process queue so the socket stays drained even if processing is slow.
- Use SSE `id:`/Last-Event-ID so reconnects can dedupe.
- Set header `Accept-Encoding: identity` to avoid intermediary gzipping which can force buffering.
Sam (ACME): We can't remove the proxy. Any server-side toggles you can try for us?
Priya (runtime): We can enable a few org-scoped flags for your account:
- `soft_close`: send periodic `: keepalive
` comments (every 15s) to coax proxies to flush rather than buffer.
- `last_event_id_strict`: include explicit `id:` fields and send a header to help clients dedupe on reconnects.
- increase backpressure timeout for your org (risk: long-slow clients may consume worker capacity).
Wel need your org id + a low-traffic window to flip canary flags.
Maya (support): I can file an internal change request and schedule a canary. Sam, share your org id and a test window. Also, try the minimal aggressive-reader node snippet below to make your consumer read bytes quickly and push work into a separate worker thread:
```
const https = require('https');
const url = process.env.URL;
https.get(url, {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.TOKEN}`, Accept: 'text/event-stream', 'Accept-Encoding': 'identity'}}, res => {
  res.on('data', chunk => {
    // quick: push chunk into a ring buffer or queue, return immediately
  });
});
```
Sam (ACME): Org id: acme-org-42. Test window: 02:30-03:30 UTC tomorrow.
Maya (support): Filing ticket now. Ticket SUP-4129. Requesting `soft_close` + `last_event_id_strict` for acme-org-42 during your window and will canary to dev first.
deploy-bot: change rolled to dev: enable soft_close and last_event_id_strict for acme-org-42 2026-03-16T02:30:00Z -> 2026-03-16T04:00:00Z (canary). Monitor: /ops/streaming/backpressure
Luis (backend): Follow-up for eng: we should emit a `partial_chunk` marker if we close mid-event so clients can detect truncation and ask server to resend last id on reconnect. Also wel add a `client_slow_consumer` metric and alert so support can proactively reach out.
Sam (ACME): I'll run tests during the window and report results. Thanks for the quick triage.
Maya (support): Please ping this thread with the pcap and any client-side logs if you still see ECONNRESET or duplicated events. If duplication persists we'll escalate to eng-runtime for deeper tracing. :thumbsup:
